```{r setup}
set.seed(31102022)
n.simulations <- 1e6
```  

# 1. Two Fair Games

```{r game-setup}
num.attempts <- 20
simulate.game <- function(outcomes,probabilities,reps=10^(1:5)){
  for(repetitions in reps){
    total.in.game.runs <- replicate(num.attempts,
                                sum(sample(outcomes,repetitions,TRUE,probabilities)))
    cat(paste0("The total gain in ",as.integer(repetitions)," plays may be:\n"))
    cat(total.in.game.runs)
    cat("\n\n")
  }
}
```  

Game 1:
```{r game-1}
outcomes.1 <- c(-1,1)
probs.1 <- c(0.5,0.5)
cat(paste("Expectation in Game 1 is",sum(outcomes.1*probs.1)))
simulate.game(outcomes.1,probs.1)
```   

Game 3:
```{r game-3}
outcomes.3 <- c(-999,1)
probs.3 <- c(0.001,0.999)
cat(paste("Expectation in Game 3 is",sum(outcomes.3*probs.3)))
simulate.game(outcomes.3,probs.3)
```   

# 2. Expectation and Variance Example

This example continues Exercise 5(i), Week 2.
```{r ex5(i)-wk2-analytical}
x<-c(0,1,2,3)
p<-c(0.125,0.375,0.375,0.125)
(EX <- sum(x*p))
sum((x-EX)^2*p)
sum(x^2*p) - (EX)^2
``` 

We can obtain (approximately) the same results by simulations:
```{r ex5(i)-wk2-simulations}
sample.example <- sample(x,n.simulations,replace=TRUE,prob=p)
mean(sample.example)
var(sample.example)
```   

# 3. Expectation and Variance: Sample from a Population

```{r pop-set}
population.size <- 1e4
population.IQ <- rnorm(population.size,100,15)
cat(paste0("Population IQ expectation: ",mean(population.IQ),
           "\n Population IQ variance: ",var(population.IQ),
           "\n Population IQ standard deviation: ",sd(population.IQ)))
```  

Let's simulate sampling without replacement from a population (note that this does not give us a hypergeometric distribution as we sample real numbers, not 0s and 1s):
```{r pop-sample}
small.sample.size <- 20
for(i in 1:5){
  sample.IQ <- sample(population.IQ,small.sample.size,replace=FALSE)
  cat(paste0("Sample IQ expectation: ",mean(sample.IQ),"\n",
             "Sample IQ variance: ",var(sample.IQ),"\n",
             "Sample IQ standard deviation: ",sd(sample.IQ),"\n\n"))
}
```  

The next comparison demonstrates the effect of the finite population correction (FPC). 
The variance of the sample mean is equal to the population variance divided by the sample size and multiplied 
by the FPC:
```{r pop-samples-small-and-large}
# this simulation is slow as it is not implemented efficiently!
n.sim <- 1e4
cat(paste0("The variance of the mean for a small sample is: ",
           small.sample.size *
             var(replicate(n.sim,mean(sample(population.IQ,small.sample.size,replace=FALSE)))),"\n"))

large.sample.size <- population.size/2
cat(paste0("The variance of the mean for a large sample is: ",
           large.sample.size *
             var(replicate(n.sim,mean(sample(population.IQ,large.sample.size,replace=FALSE)))),"\n"))
```  

# 4. Distributions, Expectations and Variances

Let's plot several distributions and their respective expectations and standard deviations.
```{r settings}
prob <- c(0.5,0.4,0.3,0.2,0.1,0.05)
size <- 100
population <- 200
```  

### Binomial Distribution

```{r binom,fig.width=10,fig.height=10}
par(mfrow=c(3,2))
for (p in prob){
  binom.mean <- size*p
  binom.std <- sqrt(size*p*(1-p))
  bounds <- binom.mean + c(-1,0,1)*binom.std
  sample <- rbinom(n.simulations,size,p)
  hist(sample,breaks=0:size,main=paste("Binomial p=",p,sep=""),
       xlab=paste("range: ",paste0(range(sample),collapse=" - "),
                  ", outside blue: ",
                  length(sample[sample<bounds[1] | sample>bounds[3]])/n.simulations*100,
                  "%","\n",
                  "Mean: ",round(mean(sample),digits=3)," vs. ",
                  round(bounds[2],digits=3),
                  "; St. Dev.: ",round(sd(sample),digits=3)," vs. ",
                  round(bounds[3]-bounds[2],digits=3)));
  abline(v=bounds[2],col="red");
  abline(v=bounds[1],col="blue");abline(v=bounds[3],col="blue")
}
```   

### Hypergeometric Distribution

```{r hyper,fig.width=10,fig.height=10}
par(mfrow=c(3,2))
for (p in prob){
  hg.mean <- size*p
  hg.std <- sqrt(size*p*(1-p)*(1-(size-1)/(population-1)))
  bounds <- hg.mean + c(-1,0,1)*hg.std
  sample <- rhyper(n.simulations,p*population,(1-p)*population,size)
  hist(sample,breaks=0:size,
       main=paste("Hypergeometric M=",p*population," N=",population,sep=""),
       xlab=paste("range: ",paste0(range(sample),collapse=" - "),
                  ", outside blue: ",
                  length(sample[sample<bounds[1] | sample>bounds[3]])/n.simulations*100,
                  "%","\n",
                  "Mean: ",round(mean(sample),digits=3)," vs. ",
                  round(bounds[2],digits=3),
                  "; St. Dev.: ",round(sd(sample),digits=3)," vs. ",
                  round(bounds[3]-bounds[2],digits=3)));
  abline(v=bounds[2],col="red");
  abline(v=bounds[1],col="blue");abline(v=bounds[3],col="blue")
}
```   

### Exponential Distribution

```{r exp,fig.width=10,fig.height=10}
lambda <- prob*size
par(mfrow=c(3,2))
for (l in lambda){
  exp.mean <- 1/l
  exp.std <- 1/l
  bounds <- exp.mean + c(-1,0,1)*exp.std
  sample <- rexp(n.simulations,l)
  range.sample <- range(sample)
  hist(sample,breaks=round(5*(range.sample[2]-range.sample[1])/exp.std),
       main=paste("Exponential lambda=",l,sep=""),
       xlab=paste("range: ",paste0(round(range.sample,digits=6),collapse=" - "),
                  ", outside blue: ",
                  length(sample[sample<bounds[1] | sample>bounds[3]])/n.simulations*100,
                  "%","\n",
                  "Mean: ",round(mean(sample),digits=3)," vs. ",
                  round(bounds[2],digits=3),
                  "; St. Dev.: ",round(sd(sample),digits=3)," vs. ",
                  round(bounds[3]-bounds[2],digits=3)));
  abline(v=bounds[2],col="red");
  abline(v=bounds[1],col="blue");abline(v=bounds[3],col="blue")
}
```   


# 5. Expectation and Variance: (In)dependent Variables

Let's simulate values of several random variables and estimate their mean and variance from the simulated values. 

```{r}
X <- rpois(n.simulations,2) 
# random values from a Poisson distribution, for no particular reason
Y <- rpois(n.simulations,3)
Z <- 2*X
W <- X+Y
U <- Z+W
my.format <- function(data){
  paste(
    paste0("mean ",round(mean(data),digits=2),","),
    paste0("variance  ",round(var(data),digits=1),","),
    paste0("std ",round(sd(data),digits=3)),
    sep="\t\t")
}
cat(paste0(
  paste0("X:     ",my.format(X),"\n"),
  paste0("Y:     ",my.format(Y),"\n"),
  paste0("Z=2X:  ",my.format(Z),"\n"),
  paste0("W=X+Y: ",my.format(W),"\n"),
  paste0("U=Z+W: ",my.format(U),"\n")
))
```
